metadata.description: Diagnoses common vehicle starting and performance issues

rules.explanation: If the car won't start and is completely silent (no clicking), the battery is likely dead.
Rapid clicking sounds usually indicate the starter motor or a weak battery.
If it cranks (engine turns over) and has fuel, it might be an ignition issue.
The engine cannot run without fuel. This is a common oversight.
A rough idle with a check engine light often points to air intake sensor issues.

questions.car_wont_start: Is the car failing to start the engine?
questions.silent_start: When you turn the key/press start, is it completely silent (no sounds)?
questions.clicking_sound: Do you hear a rapid clicking noise when trying to start?
questions.cranks_but_no_start: Does the engine make a 'chug-chug' sound (cranking) but fails to run?
questions.has_fuel: Does the fuel gauge show that the tank has gas?
questions.no_fuel: Is the fuel tank empty or near empty?
questions.engine_check_light: Is the 'Check Engine' light illuminated on the dashboard?
questions.rough_idle: Does the engine shake or feel 'rough' when the car is stopped?

check_battery.text: The battery is likely dead. Try jump-starting the car or replace the battery.

check_starter.text: The starter motor might be stuck or the battery is too weak. Check battery terminals first.

check_spark_plugs.text: Inspect the spark plugs and ignition coils. They may need replacement.

add_fuel.text: Add fuel to the tank. It seems you ran out of gas.

check_MAF_sensor.text: Clean or replace the Mass Air Flow (MAF) sensor.
